note: Critical grammar spine for travel Spanish (Mexico). Decomposed into rungs, ordered by the sequencer (leverage + prereqs + structure rotation). Rungs ride the same FSRS + taper machinery as vocabulary.

present.title: Present tense
present.about: Regular verb endings for who's doing it.

copula.title: ser vs estar
copula.about: The two ways to say 'to be'.

rungs.title: Present tense: I & you
rungs.teach:
Regular verbs change their ending to say who. For **I**, use **-o**; for **you**, **-as** (-ar verbs) or **-es** (-er/-ir verbs).

• hablar → hablo / hablas (I speak / you speak)
• comer → como / comes (I eat / you eat)

Drop the pronoun — the ending already says who.

rungs.title: tú vs usted
rungs.teach:
Spanish has two “you”s. Use **tú** with friends, kids, and peers. Use **usted** — the polite one — with strangers, elders, and anyone serving you.

Usted takes the “he/she” verb form:
• ¿cómo estás? (tú) → **¿cómo está?** (usted)
• ¿hablas inglés? → **¿habla inglés?**

When in doubt, use usted.

quiz.prompt: Talking to a shopkeeper you just met, use…

rungs.title: el / la and matching words
rungs.teach:
Nouns are masculine (**el / un**) or feminine (**la / una**) — usually **-o** vs **-a**.

• el taxi, un café  ·  la cuenta, una cerveza

Adjectives agree and usually come **after** the noun: agua frí**a**, café calien**te**.

quiz.prompt: Put it in Spanish order: “cold water”

rungs.title: Word order & saying “no”
rungs.teach:
Order is like English: subject–verb–object, and you can drop the subject — **quiero café** (I want coffee).

To say **not**, put **no** right before the verb:
• no entiendo (I don't understand)
• no quiero (I don't want)

rungs.title: The going-to future: voy a
rungs.teach:
For what you're about to do, use **voy a** + a verb (its plain -ar/-er/-ir form):

• voy a comer (I'm going to eat)
• voy a pagar (I'm going to pay)

One little phrase buys you the whole future — no new endings.

examples.english: I'm going to pay by card

rungs.title: Understanding he/she/we
rungs.teach:
You'll hear these in answers. Same regular verbs, other people:

• **-a / -e** = he, she, or polite “you” → habla, come
• **-amos / -emos** = we → hablamos, comemos

Mostly you just need to recognize them.

rungs.title: ser vs estar (both “to be”)
rungs.teach:
Two verbs mean “to be”. Simple rule of thumb:

• **ser** — who or what something *is*: soy turista, es café.
• **estar** — *where* it is and *how you feel*: está aquí, estoy bien, estoy cansado.

Location & feelings → estar.
